I hold a DTV visa at the moment but prefer to have the Thailand Elite Visa so as to be more stable for the future. Do I have to leave Thailand to get the elite visa or can I apply within Thailand?
Yes, you can apply for the Thailand Elite Visa while you are in Thailand — however, you will need to leave the country for the visa issuance.
Once your application is approved and you receive your Welcome Letter, you can have the visa affixed upon arrival at the airport when re-entering Thailand.
The approval process typically takes around 3–4 weeks, so we recommend applying in advance if your current visa is nearing expiration.
I have read that it is quite difficult now to open a bank account in Thailand. Does the Thailand Elite Visa holder have the ability to open a bank account in Thailand?
Yes, as a Thailand Elite Visa holder, you can open a bank account in Thailand. In fact, the TPC program offers streamlined banking access as one of its key privileges.
Thailand Elite has partnerships with major banks, including:

Kasikorn Bank (KBank) : Thailand Elite members can visit any KBank branch without needing an appointment to open an account. Required documents include a valid passport, Thailand Elite Visa, membership card, and a Thai mobile number. KBank also offers foreign currency deposit accounts in multiple currencies such as USD, EUR, AUD, and more.
Bangkok Bank (BBL) : Members can open accounts at any Bangkok Bank branch. However, you’ll need to make a reservation through the Member Contact Center at least five working days in advance.
To open a bank account, you’ll typically need:
-Valid passport (same as registered with Thailand Elite)
-Thailand Elite Visa
-Thailand Elite Membership Card/Certificate Letter
-Thai mobile phone number
-Details of your residence in Thailand

For a family of four planning to work remotely in Thailand, the Platinum Package (10-year visa) is the most suitable, offering family add-on pricing and long-term stability.
Special Promotion (1 July – 30 September 2025):
Additional family members applying under the Platinum, Diamond, or Reserve packages can enjoy a discounted rate of THB 500,000 (normally THB 1M–2M).

primary_content.text: What are the main features, benefits, and eligibility requirements of the Thailand Elite Visa, and how does it compare to other long-term visa options for foreigners wishing to stay in Thailand?

The Thailand Elite Visa, now called the Thailand Privilege Visa, is a long-term residency visa offering stays from 5 to 20 years, depending on the package. Key features include multiple-entry visas, concierge services, fast-track immigration, and access to exclusive benefits like airport lounges and health checkups. It requires a one-time membership fee starting at THB 650,000, with no age, income, or employment restrictions. Unlike retirement or marriage visas, it does not require financial proof, ongoing income, or Thai sponsors. However, it does not allow employment in Thailand, though remote work for foreign companies is permitted. Compared to other long-term visas, it offers greater convenience, fewer bureaucratic steps, and is ideal for high-net-worth individuals or remote workers seeking a premium lifestyle. It’s more expensive but far more flexible and hassle-free than retirement or Non-immigrant O visas.
I have a family member married to a Thai woman. They would like to be together. He is 63 and a US citizen. Which VISA option is best for this situation?
If your 63-year-old US citizen family member prefers the Thailand Elite Visa route, the best option is the Bronze Membership:
– THB 650,000 for a 5-year visa
– Easiest, most affordable Elite option
– No age or income requirements
– Fast-track services, immigration support
– No need to show financial proof like the Thai Marriage Visa
This is the best long term visa option if he wants convenience, minimal paperwork, and doesn’t plan to work in Thailand.

Hi Rex, if you are applying to have a Thai company/entity set up in order to conduct business but are not planning on living there (but will occasionally flying back forth) can the Thai Elite Visa be in place of a business visa?

If you will be a managing director of this Thai company, unfortunately a Thai Elite visa will not be issued to you until you remove yourself as director. Having a Thai business visa might be more suitable in your case in this occasion. However, if your part of the company does not require you to have a work permit or the participation in this Thai company is very minimal, you may apply for Thailand Elite visa for you to have a multiple entry long term visa in Thailand.

primary_content.text: Last updated: July 2026

The Thailand Elite Visa, now officially branded as the Thailand Privilege Visa, remains one of Thailand’s most established long-term residence programs in 2026. It is designed for foreign nationals seeking predictable, compliant, and uninterrupted residency in Thailand. Applicants can now secure their long-term stay through five updated membership tiers: Bronze, Gold, Platinum, Diamond, and Reserve.

main_topic.h_title: What’s New for 2026
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: The following updates apply to Thailand Elite Visa applications in 2026:
The Bronze membership application period has been extended until 30 September 2026
Immigration screening and background checks remain in place for the Thailand Privilege Card, with processing timelines varying by nationality
Take advantage of the extended application window and secure your membership benefits before the promotion period ends. Submit your application today.
Legacy Thailand Elite packages have been replaced under the current Thailand Privilege membership structure, as outlined below.

Note: Existing Thailand Elite Visa holders retain their original rights and visa validity. New applicants looking to apply for the Thailand Elite Visa must proceed under the current Thailand Privilege Card program.

urls.anchor_text: apply for the Thailand Elite Visa

main_topic.h_title: The Thailand Elite Visa at a Glance
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Visa Type: A long-term, multiple-entry visa allowing residence in Thailand for 5, 10, 15, or 20 years, depending on the Thailand Privilege Card membership tier.
Cost: A one-time membership fee ranging from 650,000 THB to 5,000,000 THB.

Key Benefits: A simplified stay in Thailand without frequent renewals, VIP fast-track airport services, dedicated concierge support for government procedures, and access to exclusive lifestyle privileges through the Thailand Privilege Visa points system.

In 2026, the program will be widely used by long-stay residents, retirees and global citizens who want to base themselves in Thailand with predictable residency and minimal administrative burden. The Thailand Privilege Card provides an alternative without the annual renewals, financial maintenance rules, or employer sponsorship required by many other long-stay visas.

main_topic.h_title: Why Choose the Thailand Privilege Visa?
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: While there are other options for staying in Thailand, the Thailand Privilege Visa remains the top choice for expats who value convenience and flexibility.

main_topic.h_title: 1. Guaranteed Long-Term Residency
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: The core benefit of the Thailand Elite Visa is the 5-year renewable multi-entry visa. Depending on your Thailand Privilege Card membership tier, you will receive a validity of 5, 10, 15, or 20 years.
No Re-Entry Permits: You can leave and enter Thailand as many times as you like. The Thailand Privilege Visa is automatically stamped for a 1-year stay upon every arrival.

Uninterrupted Stay: If you choose not to travel, you can stay in Thailand continuously without ever leaving. (You simply extend your Thailand Elite Visa stay at a local immigration office once per year).

main_topic.h_title: 2. VIP Airport Fast-Track Service
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Thailand is one of the world’s most popular travel destinations, meaning airport immigration queues can often take over an hour.

Arrival: As a Thailand Privilege Card member, you are greeted at the airbridge by an Elite Personal Assistant (EPA) holding a signboard with your name. You are escorted via electric cart to the Premium Immigration Lane, bypassing the tourist queues.
Departure: You enjoy the same fast-track service and access to exclusive airport lounges while waiting for your flight under the Thailand Privilege Visa program.

main_topic.h_title: 3. The “Government Concierge” (Elite Personal Liaison)
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Bureaucracy in a foreign country can be daunting. Thailand Privilege Card members have access to the Elite Personal Liaison (EPL) service.

90-Day Reporting: For members living in Bangkok, Chiang Mai, Pattaya, or Phuket, you can drop off your passport at the Thailand Elite Visa office, and the staff will handle your mandatory 90-day reporting for you free of charge.

Bank Accounts: Opening a bank account as a foreigner can be difficult. Thailand Privilege Visa members receive a letter of recommendation facilitating the opening of multi-currency accounts (USD, EUR, THB) with Bangkok Bank or Kasikorn Bank.
Driver’s License: Liaison staff can assist Thailand Privilege Card holders in the process of obtaining a Thai driving license.

main_topic.h_title: 4. The New “Privilege Points” System (2026 Update)
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: A major upgrade for the 2026 program is the introduction of Privilege Points for the Thailand Privilege Visa. Unlike the old system, where benefits were static, members now receive an annual allocation of points to “spend” on lifestyle perks tailored to their needs through their Thailand Privilege Card.

Redeemable Perks Include: Domestic round-trip flights, 5-star hotel buffet vouchers, extensive health checkups, golf green fees, spa treatments, and private airport transfers for Thailand Elite Visa members.

main_topic.h_title: Bronze Membership (5 Years)
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Status: Limited Time Offer (Applications close March 31, 2026)
Membership Fee: 650,000 THB (approx. $19,000 USD)
Visa Validity: 5 Years
Privilege Points: None

Who is this for? The Bronze tier is the “entry-level” Thailand Elite Visa option. It is perfect for applicants who purely want the visa residency rights and airport fast-track service but do not care about lifestyle perks like free golf or spa treatments. It is the most cost-effective way to secure a 5-year stay with a Thailand Privilege Card.

main_topic.h_title: Gold Membership (5 Years)
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Membership Fee: 900,000 THB (approx. $26,000 USD)
Visa Validity: 5 Years
Privilege Points: 20 Points / Year

Who is this for? The Gold Membership is designed for digital nomads and solo travellers who want to experience the “high life” in Thailand via their Thailand Privilege Visa. The 20 annual points on this Thailand Privilege Card are enough to cover several airport transfers or spa sessions, adding a layer of luxury to your residency.
Upgrade Path: Unlike Bronze, Gold members can upgrade to longer-term tiers (Platinum, Diamond, etc.) in the future by paying the difference plus a small fee to the Thailand Elite Visa office.

main_topic.h_title: Platinum Membership (10 Years)
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Membership Fee: 1.5 Million THB (approx. $43,000 USD)
Additional Family Member: 1 Million THB
Visa Validity: 10 Years (Two 5-year stickers)
Privilege Points: 35 Points / Year
Who is this for? This is the “sweet spot” for families and long-term expats seeking a Thailand Privilege Visa. It offers a decade of security.

main_topic.h_title: Diamond Membership (15 Years)
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Membership Fee: 2.5 Million THB (approx. $72,000 USD)
Additional Family Member: 1.5 Million THB
Visa Validity: 15 Years (Three 5-year stickers)
Privilege Points: 55 Points / Year

Who is this for? Diamond is ideal for early retirees (under age 50) who want a long-term Thailand Elite Visa solution without the hassle of annual retirement visa renewals. The 55 annual points on this Thailand Privilege Card are substantial enough to cover annual domestic flights and comprehensive health checkups at top hospitals like Bumrungrad.

main_topic.h_title: Reserve Membership (20 Years)
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Membership Fee: 5 Million THB (approx. $144,000 USD)
Additional Family Member: 2.5 Million THB
Visa Validity: 20 Years (Four 5-year stickers)
Privilege Points: 120 Points / Year

Who is this for? The Reserve is an exclusive tier for Ultra-High-Net-Worth Individuals holding a Thailand Privilege Visa. It functions as a status symbol in Thailand. Thailand Privilege Card members gain access to “The Reserve Club,” priority booking for services, supercar test drives, and the highest allocation of points.

main_topic.h_title: Thailand Privilege Benefits and Points System
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Beyond its core advantages, the Thailand Privilege Visa includes a structured benefits program designed to support daily living in Thailand as well as travel and lifestyle convenience. Benefits are organised across five core areas and redeemed through an annual Privilege Points system, allowing members to select services based on how they live and travel with their Thailand Privilege Card.

The main benefit areas include Stay, Travel, Leisure, Health and Well-Being, and Wealth. Together, these cover hotel and dining privileges, Fast Track immigration services, airport transfers and lounge access, golf and cultural activities, medical and wellness services, and selected business or wealth-related offerings available to Thailand Privilege Visa members.

Eligible membership tiers (Gold and above) receive an annual allocation of Privilege Points, which can be redeemed through the official Thailand Privilege Card application rather than receiving a fixed set of predefined perks.

main_topic.h_title: How the Thailand Privilege Points System Works
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Privilege Points are credited annually and redeemed through the official Thailand Privilege Card system. To provide a practical reference point, points are commonly used for the following types of services:
This points-based structure allows Thailand Privilege Visa members to allocate benefits each year based on their current lifestyle needs rather than a fixed package of perks.

row_cells.text: Airport transfers, airport lounge access, spa sessions, hotel dining, Elite Personal Liaison support for 90-day reporting and basic immigration tasks
Golf sessions, dental checkups, assistance opening a Thai bank account, assistance obtaining a Thai driving licence
Domestic round-trip flights, annual health checkups, wellness programs, private tours, and selected special activities

main_topic.h_title: Who the Thailand Privilege Visa Is For
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: The Thailand Privilege Visa is intended for people seeking long-term residency stability, not short visits. Typical applicants for the Thailand Elite Visa are:
Individuals looking for long-term residency with minimal government and administrative requirements
Retirees who prefer not to manage annual retirement visa renewals
Foreign nationals living in Thailand while earning income abroad
Families seeking a predictable long-term immigration status through the Thailand Privilege Card

main_topic.h_title: Example 1: Long-stay life in Bangkok
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Many Thailand Privilege Visa members use the visa to base themselves in Bangkok while travelling frequently in the region. For example, a consultant might rent a condo near BTS Asok on a one-year lease, open a bank account with a Thai bank on Sukhumvit, and sign up for a local mobile plan using their Thailand Privilege Card documents. With a long-term, multiple-entry visa, they can fly to Singapore, Hong Kong, or Europe several times a year and still re-enter Thailand through the fast-track Elite immigration lane at Suvarnabhumi, avoiding long queues on each trip.

main_topic.h_title: Example 2: Retiree in Chiang Mai managing immigration
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: A retiree who wants to live in Chiang Mai full-time often worries about annual extensions, financial requirements, and unexpected changes to retirement visa extensions. By switching to a Thailand Privilege Visa membership, they hold a 5–15 year visa and use the Elite service team to handle most interactions with Chiang Mai immigration. The Thailand Privilege Card member still completes 90-day reporting, but with guidance and support, and does not have to show annual financial evidence in a Thai bank the way a standard retirement visa often requires. This simplifies long-term planning for Thailand Elite Visa holders.

main_topic.h_title: Example 3: Family based in Phuket or Pattaya
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Some members use the Thailand Privilege Visa to base their family in Phuket or Pattaya while one partner commutes internationally for work. The primary member and their dependents can live in a villa or condo near the beach, enrol their children in an international school, and rely on the Elite concierge for airport transfers and immigration support via the Thailand Privilege Card. Because the visa is long-term and multiple-entry, the commuting partner can fly in and out of Thailand regularly without worrying about re-entry permits or constant visa extensions.

main_topic.h_title: Example 4: Digital nomad or remote worker in Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Although the Thailand Elite Visa is not a work permit, many remote workers and business owners use it while working for foreign companies from Thailand. A digital nomad might spend six months in Bangkok and six months in Chiang Mai each year using their Thailand Privilege Card. The long-term Thailand Privilege Visa means they do not need to switch between short-stay visas or worry about frequent border runs, and they still benefit from fast-track immigration and concierge services at Thai airports when they travel.

main_topic.h_title: Thailand Privilege Visa Eligibility
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: To be eligible for the Thailand Privilege Card membership program, applicants must meet the following criteria:
Possess a valid foreign passport with a minimum of one year remaining before expiration
Have no history of serious visa overstays in Thailand
Have no criminal record, bankruptcy status, or legal declaration of mental incapacity
Not currently holding, nor have previously held, a Thailand Volunteer Visa
Note: Applicants holding an Education Visa may still apply for the Thailand Elite Visa, but will be required to provide additional supporting documentation to the Thailand Privilege Visa office.

main_topic.h_title: Thailand Elite Visa Application Process
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Before submitting an application, it is recommended to consult an authorised General Sales and Services Agent (GSSA). Application assistance for the Thailand Privilege Card is provided free of charge. The complete Thailand Elite Visa application process generally requires between 1 and 3 months, depending on screening and processing timelines.

row_cells.text: Applicants submit a completed Thailand Privilege Card application form.
Thai Immigration conducts checks for the Thailand Privilege Visa.
The Thailand Elite Visa fee is paid directly to the program office.
Thailand Privilege issues the Membership ID and welcome letter.
The Thailand Privilege Visa is affixed to the passport.

main_topic.h_title: Where the Thailand Elite Visa Can Be Issued
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Major international airports where Thailand Privilege Visa issuance is available include Suvarnabhumi Airport, Don Mueang International Airport, Chiang Mai International Airport, and Phuket International Airport.

main_topic.h_title: Already in Thailand? How to Switch to the Thailand Elite Visa
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Many foreign nationals first learn about the Thailand Elite Visa while they are already in Thailand on a Tourist Visa or visa-exempt entry. Unlike most long-stay visa options, the Thailand Privilege Card allows eligible applicants to complete the process inside Thailand, without the need for international travel, provided timing requirements are met.

main_topic.h_title: Affixing Your Thailand Elite Visa at Chaeng Wattana (No Flights Required)
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: If you are currently in Thailand on a Tourist Visa (TR) or a Visa Exemption entry and still have at least 30 days of remaining permission to stay, you may be eligible to convert your status without leaving the country.
Once membership approval is issued, the Thailand Privilege Visa can be affixed locally at the Immigration Bureau at Chaeng Wattana in Bangkok, rather than at a Thai embassy or consulate abroad.
In practical terms, this means:
No visa run to a neighbouring country
No embassy or consulate appointment overseas
No disruption to your stay in Thailand

An Elite Personal Assistant (EPA) arranges the Chaeng Wattana appointment in advance and accompanies the member on the day of visa affixation. Documentation is processed through the dedicated Elite channel, allowing the visa to be placed in the passport without joining standard immigration queues. This option is commonly used by applicants already living in Bangkok or nearby provinces.

main_topic.h_title: Life in Thailand After Thailand Privilege Visa Approval
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Once your Thailand Privilege Card has been issued, daily life in Thailand becomes easier to manage, particularly for immigration procedures and administrative tasks that apply to long-stay residents.

main_topic.h_title: VIP 90-Day Reporting
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Passport Drop-Off at Sathorn and Chamchuri Square

All foreign nationals staying long-term in Thailand must complete 90-day reporting. Thailand Privilege Card members in Bangkok have access to a simplified alternative to visiting immigration offices in person.
Members may use the Elite Visa 90-day report passport drop-off service at designated Thailand Privilege locations, including:
Thailand Privilege Head Office, Sathorn
Chamchuri Square, Bangkok

Passports are submitted at the selected drop-off point and returned once reporting has been completed. Elite Personal Assistants coordinate scheduling and submission, allowing members to avoid queues at Chaeng Wattana and handle reporting as part of a predictable routine.
This service is particularly valuable for members who live in Bangkok year-round or travel frequently.

main_topic.h_title: Opening a Thai Bank Account
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Bangkok Bank Silom Head Office Fast-Track

Opening a full Thai bank account can be difficult on short-stay visas. After long-term status is established through the Thailand Privilege Card, many members are able to open accounts at the Bangkok Bank Head Office on Silom Road, where Elite members are fast-tracked.
At the Silom Head Office, members commonly open:
A Thai baht savings account for everyday use
A Foreign Currency Deposit (FCD) account to hold USD, EUR, or GBP locally

An Elite Personal Assistant may accompany the member to the Bangkok Bank Silom Head Office to help coordinate documentation and streamline the process, which is often completed more efficiently than at standard retail branches.

main_topic.h_title: Ongoing Immigration Support and Practical Assistance
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Thailand Privilege Card members remain subject to standard immigration requirements, including TM.30 address notifications and reporting obligations. The advantage of the program lies in access to structured, ongoing support.
Elite Personal Assistants help members:
Understand reporting timelines
Coordinate submissions
Reduce the risk of missed deadlines
This support is particularly useful for members who move residences, travel frequently, or divide their time between Thailand and other countries.

main_topic.h_title: Tax Residency and Compliance
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Holding a Thailand Privilege Visa does not automatically make a member a Thai tax resident. Tax residency in Thailand is generally determined by physical presence, with 180 days or more in Thailand during a calendar year commonly used as the reference point.

The key advantage of the Thailand Privilege Visa is residency stability. This allows members to plan ahead and, where appropriate, request assistance from an Elite Personal Assistant in coordinating the application for a Thai Tax Identification Number (TIN) with the Revenue Department, based on individual circumstances.

main_topic.h_title: Thai Driving Licence Application
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Many Thailand Privilege Card members choose to obtain a Thai driving licence after settling in Thailand. This process is handled through the Department of Land Transport once residency documentation is established.

A Thai driving licence is widely used for insurance coverage, vehicle rental, and everyday identification. Elite Personal Assistants may help coordinate appointments and documentation, making the process easier to navigate for members living in Thailand full-time.

main_topic.h_title: Thailand Privilege Visa Compared With Other Long-Stay Visas
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Each long-stay visa in Thailand serves a different purpose. The Thailand Privilege Visa is typically chosen by residents who prioritise long-term certainty and reduced administrative burden. The Thailand Elite Visa remains the most flexible option.

row_cells.text: Upfront membership fee; background check; valid passport
Issued for 5–20 years depending on tier; no age or income requirement; no annual renewals; does not itself grant work rights; includes immigration and administrative support
Age 50+; financial evidence (bank balance or income); annual extension
Must renew yearly; funds must be maintained in a Thai bank account
High income thresholds, assets, or professional credentials
Strict eligibility; limited applicant pool; offers work and tax benefits for approved cases
Legal marriage; financial requirements; relationship documentation
Annual renewals; ongoing proof of relationship, finances, and location
Proof of qualifying activity (remote work, training, cultural programs)
Fixed scope and duration; residence; not allowed to open a Thai bank account

main_topic.h_title: Is the Thailand Elite Visa still available in 2026?
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Yes. The Thailand Elite Visa is still available in 2026, but it is now officially called the Thailand Privilege Visa. The program continues under Thailand Privilege Card Co., Ltd.

main_topic.h_title: How do I apply for a Thailand Elite Visa in 2026?
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Applying for the Thailand Elite Visa involves a simple four-step process: (1) Select your membership tier (Bronze, Gold, Platinum, Diamond, or Reserve), (2) Submit a passport copy and application form for background screening, (3) Pay the membership fee upon approval, and (4) Affix your visa at a Thai embassy, the airport, or at immigration.

main_topic.h_title: Who is eligible for the Thailand Elite Visa?
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: The Thailand Elite Visa is available to foreign nationals who hold a valid passport, have no serious immigration overstays, and pass background checks. There are no minimum income requirements for the Thailand Privilege Visa.

main_topic.h_title: How long does it take to get a Thailand Elite Visa?
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: The process typically takes 1 to 3 months. Once approved, you receive your Thailand Privilege Card and can have the Thailand Privilege Visa affixed.

main_topic.h_title: How long can you stay in Thailand with a Thailand Elite Visa?
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Depending on the package, long-term stay options include 5, 10, 15, or 20 years with a Thailand Privilege Visa.

main_topic.h_title: Where do I get the Thailand Elite Visa stamped?
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: The Thailand Privilege Visa can be affixed in Bangkok (Chaeng Wattana), at a Royal Thai embassy abroad, or on arrival at selected international airports with Thailand Privilege Card support.

main_topic.h_title: Is the Thailand Elite Visa being discontinued?
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: No. The Thailand Elite Visa has been rebranded as the Thailand Privilege Visa, but it remains active.

main_topic.h_title: What is the longest visa you can get for Thailand?
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: The Thailand Privilege Visa currently offers up to 20 years of residency through its highest Thailand Privilege Card membership tiers.

main_topic.h_title: What is the 10-year “Golden Visa” for Thailand?
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: This commonly refers to either the Thailand Privilege Visa (10-year Platinum tier) or the LTR Visa.

main_topic.h_title: Can I work in Thailand on the Thailand Elite Visa?
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: No. The Thailand Elite Visa does not grant work authorisation. Members need a separate work permit to work for a Thai company with their Thailand Privilege Card. However, remote work for employers or clients located outside Thailand is permitted, provided no Thai income source or local employment is involved.

main_topic.h_title: Can I buy property in Thailand with a Thailand Elite Visa?
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Thailand Elite Visa holders may purchase condominiums in their own name under existing foreign ownership rules via the Thailand Privilege Card.

main_topic.h_title: Can I bring my family with a Thailand Elite Visa?
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Yes. Certain Thailand Privilege Card tiers allow family members to be added to the Thailand Privilege Visa.

main_topic.h_title: Is the Thailand Elite Visa worth the cost?
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: The Thailand Privilege Visa is considered valuable by long-term residents who want stability and reduced administration through the Thailand Privilege Card.

main_topic.h_title: What is the difference between a Thailand retirement visa and the Elite Visa?
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: A retirement visa requires being 50+ and has annual renewals. The Thailand Elite Visa has no age requirements and is issued via a one-time fee for the Thailand Privilege Visa.
